_comment: Single source of truth for the Diplomatic Hall floor plan. Read by scripts/build_venue.py (Blender: geometry baked into the GLB) and by src/main.js (interaction, collision, minimap). Coordinates are three.js world metres: x east, z = -(Blender y), y up. The stage is at the north end (most negative z); the main entrance is on the south wall at z = 0.

hall._comment: The authoring .blend is a 19.35 x 25.15 m hall with a 3.5 m ceiling. The build stretches every vertex north of stretchFromZ by stretchBy (keeping the chamfered stage-end corners and every door where they were) and lifts every vertex above ceilingFrom by ceilingBy.

led._comment: 16:9 LED wall standing on the back of the stage. 10.0 x 5.625 m — twice the area of the old 7 x 3.94 m screen.

seating._comment: Twenty seats: one row of ten either side of a 2.4 m centre aisle, facing the stage.

clusters._comment: Eight clusters of three booths (24 booths), laid out 3-2-3 as in the venue floor plan and grouped by theme. Counting starts at the front row (by the stage) and runs C1 -> C8; within a cluster the two stage-facing bays take the lower numbers. `booths` lists the official booth numbers in bay order. Each cluster is three 1.0 x 2.4 m partition panels radiating from a hub at 120 deg; every panel is shared back to back by two booths. panelAngles are degrees in the x/z plane measured from +x toward +z (so -90 points north at the stage). A booth is the bay between two panels; bays are listed in booth order.

graphic._comment: Printable area of one panel face: radial span from the hub, height span, and offset from the panel's centre plane (the fabric core is ±0.015; the extra ~8 mm clears meshopt position quantization in the GLB).

counter._comment: Counter in the bay's own frame: radial depth span, half width, height.

standees._comment: Freestanding cut-outs from the stage design, placed on the hall floor either side of the stage so they never cover the LED wall.
